input:
Staff Data Platform Engineer, Clinical Research

Litware Biosciences - Boulder, CO

About Litware Biosciences
Litware Biosciences runs early-phase oncology trials across eleven partner sites
and builds the data systems those trials depend on. Our platform group owns
ingestion from laboratory instruments and electronic data capture, the warehouse
our biostatisticians query, and the audit trail that regulators and sponsors read
when they inspect a study. We publish our methods, we share tooling with our
partner sites, and we treat the people who enter data at those sites as the users
who matter most.

Over the last two years the platform has grown from four studies to nineteen. The
ingestion layer that served the first four was written in a hurry, and it now
carries more load and more regulated history than it was designed for. We are
hiring a staff engineer to set the technical direction for that platform over the
next three years and to lead the rebuild without interrupting a single study.

About the team
The platform team is nine engineers and two data managers, with a product lead
who came from clinical operations. We work closely with biostatistics, with the
quality group that owns our validation evidence, and with the site support team
that answers calls from coordinators. Most of the team has been here for more
than three years, and we would like that to stay true.

Our partner sites range from a university cancer center with its own informatics
group to a two-room community clinic where one coordinator enters every value by
hand. The platform has to work for both. When a site goes offline for a day, its
data has to arrive intact when the connection returns, and when a site changes its
laboratory vendor, the change has to reach the warehouse without a study team
noticing anything but a note in the release log. The site support team hears
about every rough edge first, and they sit with the platform team every Thursday.

The platform today
Instrument output arrives as files dropped by vendor software onto a shared
drive, and a scheduled job sweeps that drive every fifteen minutes. Site data
arrives through our electronic data capture system, which writes to a PostgreSQL
database that the nightly batch copies into the warehouse. The warehouse is
modeled for the analyses biostatistics ran three years ago, and new studies add
tables beside the old ones rather than extending them. The audit trail is
complete, but it lives in four places, and assembling it for an inspection takes
two people most of a week. None of this is unusual for a platform that grew with
its studies, and all of it is what the next three years are for.

The problems in front of us
The first problem is latency. A coordinator who enters a lab value today cannot
see it reconciled against the instrument run until tomorrow, and a query raised
on that value waits a day longer than it needs to. The second is change. A study
amendment that adds a collected field touches the capture schema, the batch, and
the warehouse, and each of those changes is reviewed and validated separately.
The third is evidence. Every release needs validation evidence, and today that
evidence is written by hand after the release rather than produced by the build
that made it. We think one streaming ingestion layer with a written schema
contract answers the first two, and a build pipeline that emits its own evidence
answers the third. We would like you to test that view before you build on it.

What you will do
- Design and build streaming ingestion for instrument and site data
- Own the schema contract between the capture systems and the analysis warehouse
- Lead design reviews for changes that touch regulated records
- Partner with biostatistics to shape the analysis datasets they rely on
- Run the quarterly restore rehearsal for the trial archive
- Mentor engineers through their first designs on regulated systems
- Write the runbooks the on-call rotation depends on
- Represent the platform in sponsor technical reviews
- Retire the legacy nightly batch once streaming ingestion covers every study
- Set the testing standard for parsers that read instrument output

What success looks like in your first year
By the end of your first quarter you will have read every production incident
from the last year, met each partner site's data coordinator, and written a short
assessment of where the ingestion layer will fail first. By the end of your second
quarter the first instrument family will report through the new streaming path,
with its history reconciled against the legacy batch. By the end of the year the
legacy batch will carry no new study, the schema contract will have a written
compatibility policy that the warehouse team signed off, and the restore rehearsal
will run without anyone on the platform team touching it by hand.

Required qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in computer science, biomedical informatics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
- 7+ years of experience building production data platforms
- Expert Python for data engineering
- Advanced SQL, including query tuning on large PostgreSQL databases
- Experience designing event-driven pipelines on Kafka or a comparable streaming system
- Experience with change data capture from transactional databases
- Hands-on experience with dbt or a similar transformation framework
- Experience orchestrating batch workloads with Airflow or Dagster
- Working knowledge of columnar formats such as Parquet and Apache Arrow
- Experience operating services on Kubernetes in production
- Infrastructure as code with Terraform
- Experience designing schema evolution and compatibility rules for shared data contracts
- Experience building audit trails for regulated data
- Familiarity with 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements
- Experience implementing role-based access control for sensitive data
- Experience de-identifying patient data under HIPAA
- A track record of mentoring engineers through design and code review
- Clear technical writing, including design documents that others can review
- Comfort making decisions with incomplete information
- A habit of measuring a change before and after it ships

Preferred qualifications
- Experience with CDISC SDTM or ADaM datasets
- Experience integrating laboratory instruments or LIMS data
- Familiarity with HL7 FHIR resources
- Experience with ClickHouse or DuckDB for analytical workloads
- Experience writing property-based tests for data parsers
- Experience with OpenTelemetry tracing across data services
- Background in computerized system validation
- Experience presenting technical evidence to auditors or sponsors
- Rust or Go for performance-sensitive services
- Contributions to open-source data tooling
- Curiosity about how coordinators at a trial site actually enter data

Location and eligibility
The platform team works from our Boulder, Colorado campus. If this role is filled
remotely, you must live in Colorado, Utah, or New Mexico. If you live within 50
miles of the Boulder campus, you will work onsite three days a week. Must be
authorized to work in the United States.

How we work
We write a design document before any change that touches a regulated record, and
we review it in writing before we review it in a meeting. We keep an on-call
rotation of six engineers, with a written handover at each change of shift and a
standing rule that a page at night earns a slower morning. We run a blameless
review after every incident that reached a study, and we publish the review to
the partner sites it affected. We budget one week in six for work the team
chooses, and most of the tooling our partner sites use began in one of those
weeks.

Benefits
- Medical, dental and vision coverage starting on your first day
- 401(k) with a 4 percent employer match
- Sixteen weeks of paid parental leave
- An annual learning budget for courses and conferences

Litware Biosciences is an equal opportunity employer. We consider qualified
applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation,
gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

This role involves extended periods of computer work and occasional lifting of up to 20 pounds.
